next_state_election.name: General Election
next_state_election.source_name: Oregon Secretary of State — Upcoming Elections

glance_notes.source_name: Oregon Secretary of State — Upcoming Elections
glance_notes.text: 2026 General Election Registration Deadline: Oregon's voter registration deadline for the November 3, 2026 General Election is October 13. Online registration must be completed by 11:59 p.m., and mailed registration cards must be postmarked by October 13.

glance_notes.source_name: Oregon Secretary of State — Voting in Oregon
glance_notes.text: Oregon Votes by Mail: Oregon conducts elections primarily by mail. County election officials automatically mail a ballot to each active registered voter. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, ballots begin mailing October 14.

glance_notes.source_name: Oregon Secretary of State — Upcoming Elections
glance_notes.text: Election Day Ballot Deadline: Ballots placed in an official drop box must be received by 8:00 p.m. on November 3. Ballots returned by mail are valid if mailed by Election Day and received by the county elections office no later than November 10.

register.label: Register to Vote
register.content: Eligible Oregon residents may register online, by mail or in person at a county elections office or participating state agency. Oregon also automatically registers many eligible residents through its Motor Voter program when qualifying information is provided through the Oregon Driver and Motor Vehicle Services Division. To register, a person must be a U.S. citizen, an Oregon resident and at least 16 years old. A person may register beginning at age 16 but will not receive a ballot until an election occurring on or after the person's 18th birthday. Online registration is available through Oregon's voter registration system, with additional procedures available for applicants who do not have an Oregon driver license, permit or state identification card.
register.glance_value: Online, mail, in person and automatic Motor Voter registration
register.source_name: Oregon Secretary of State — Voter Registration
register.internal_note: Oregon permits registration beginning at age 16, but a registrant cannot vote until eligible by age. Oregon's automatic registration system uses qualifying DMV transactions. The online system can also assist applicants without Oregon DMV identification, although some applicants must print, sign and return the resulting registration card. Do not describe Motor Voter registration as eliminating the 21-day eligibility deadline for a particular election.

check_registration.label: Check Voter Registration
check_registration.content: Use Oregon's My Vote system to check whether you are registered, review or update your voter registration information and check the status of your ballot. My Vote also provides contact information for your county elections office and can locate an official ballot drop site.
check_registration.glance_value: Check registration and ballot status with My Vote
check_registration.source_name: Oregon Secretary of State — My Vote
check_registration.internal_note: The Secretary of State directly lists registration status, registration updates, ballot status, county elections contacts and ballot drop-site lookup among My Vote's functions.

deadlines.label: Registration Deadlines
deadlines.content: Oregon's voter registration deadline is 21 days before Election Day. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, the deadline is Tuesday, October 13. Online registration must be submitted no later than 11:59 p.m. Pacific Time on October 13. A paper registration card mailed by the voter must be postmarked no later than October 13. A registration card delivered in person must be received by the appropriate registration office or agency by the applicable closing time on October 13. Oregon does not provide general Election Day voter registration.
deadlines.source_name: Oregon Secretary of State — Upcoming Elections
deadlines.internal_note: The Secretary of State's official 2026 calendar and ORS 247.025 directly establish the 21-day deadline. October 13 is the deadline for the November 3 General Election. Electronic registrations are due by 11:59 p.m. Paper applications can qualify based on timely receipt or a qualifying October 13 postmark. Special rules may apply to a person who becomes a U.S. citizen or, in a presidential election, an Oregon resident after the ordinary registration deadline.

polling_place.label: Find a Ballot Drop Site
polling_place.content: Oregon conducts elections by mail rather than assigning ordinary Election Day polling places where most voters cast ballots. Registered voters receive ballots by mail and may return them by mail or at an official ballot drop site. Use My Vote or your county elections office to locate an official drop site. County elections offices are also open on Election Day to provide voter services, replacement ballots and ballot return options.
polling_place.glance_value: Use My Vote to find an official ballot drop site
polling_place.source_name: Oregon Secretary of State — My Vote
polling_place.internal_note: Do not describe Oregon as having conventional precinct polling places. Oregon is a vote-by-mail state. Official drop sites and county elections offices are the relevant in-person locations. The 2026 election calendar states that official drop sites are open until 8:00 p.m. Election Day and for a minimum of eight hours that day.

election_day.label: Election Day Voting
election_day.content: Oregon's General Election is Tuesday, November 3, 2026. Oregon conducts elections by mail, so voters generally complete ballots received through the mail rather than voting at an assigned precinct polling place. County elections offices are open from 7:00 a.m. until 8:00 p.m. on Election Day. Official ballot drop sites remain open until 8:00 p.m. Ballots returned to an official drop site must be received by 8:00 p.m. Ballots returned through the mail must be mailed no later than Election Day and received by the county elections office within seven calendar days after the election.
election_day.glance_value: Drop boxes close at 8:00 p.m.; county offices open 7:00 a.m. – 8:00 p.m.
election_day.source_name: Oregon Secretary of State — Upcoming Elections
election_day.internal_note: The official 2026 calendar confirms county clerk offices are open 7:00 a.m.-8:00 p.m. Election Day and official drop sites remain open until 8:00 p.m. A mailed ballot must have a qualifying postal indicator showing it was mailed no later than Election Day and must arrive within seven calendar days. ORS 254.470 also addresses ballots for which a postal indicator is absent or illegible.

polling_hours.label: Election Day Hours
polling_hours.content: Oregon does not use traditional statewide precinct polling hours because elections are conducted by mail. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, county elections offices are open from 7:00 a.m. until 8:00 p.m. Official ballot drop sites remain open until 8:00 p.m. and are required to be available for at least eight hours on Election Day.
polling_hours.glance_value: County offices: 7:00 a.m. – 8:00 p.m.; drop sites close at 8:00 p.m.
polling_hours.source_name: Oregon Secretary of State — 2026 Elections Calendar
polling_hours.internal_note: This section deliberately avoids calling 7:00 a.m.-8:00 p.m. Oregon's polling hours. Those are county clerk office hours on Election Day. Oregon votes by mail and uses official ballot drop sites rather than ordinary precinct polling locations.

early_voting.label: Voting Before Election Day
early_voting.content: Oregon does not use a separate traditional early-voting period because elections are conducted by mail. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, counties begin mailing ballots to active registered voters on October 14 and must generally complete regular ballot mailing by October 20. Once a voter receives a ballot, the voter may complete and return it before Election Day by mail or at an official ballot drop site. Voters who need election assistance, a replacement ballot or other in-person services may contact their county elections office.
early_voting.source_name: Oregon Secretary of State — Upcoming Elections
early_voting.internal_note: Do not impose another state's early-voting model on Oregon. The operative voting period begins as ballots are distributed. ORS 254.470 and the 2026 calendar establish October 14 as the first regular mailing date and October 20 as the ordinary last day to mail ballots. Voters without daily mail service have an earlier statutory mailing deadline.

absentee_mail.label: Vote by Mail
absentee_mail.content: Oregon conducts elections by mail, and active registered voters automatically receive ballots without needing to submit an absentee-ballot request. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, ballots begin mailing October 14. Voters may return completed ballots by mail or at an official ballot drop site. A ballot placed in an official drop box must be received by 8:00 p.m. on November 3. A ballot returned by mail may be counted if it is mailed no later than Election Day and received by the county elections office no later than November 10. Voters who lose, damage or do not receive their ballot may request a replacement ballot from their county elections office.
absentee_mail.glance_value: Ballots mailed automatically; mailing begins October 14
absentee_mail.source_name: Oregon Secretary of State — Voting in Oregon
absentee_mail.internal_note: Oregon should not be characterized merely as a no-excuse absentee state. It conducts elections by mail and automatically mails ballots to active registered voters. The 2026 calendar establishes November 10 as the last day to receive valid ballots mailed by Election Day. ORS 254.470 provides the statutory rules for ballot distribution and receipt, including treatment of an absent or illegible postal indicator.

voter_id.label: Voter Identification
voter_id.content: Oregon's vote-by-mail system does not generally require a voter to present photo identification when returning a ballot. Instead, the voter signs the ballot return identification envelope, and election officials use that signature as part of the ballot-verification process. Identification information is required when registering to vote. Depending on the registration method and available records, a registrant may provide an Oregon driver license, permit or state identification number, the last four digits of a Social Security number or follow the alternative registration procedures provided by Oregon election officials.
voter_id.glance_value: No general photo ID requirement to return a ballot
voter_id.source_name: Oregon Secretary of State — Voter Registration
voter_id.internal_note: Oregon's ballot authentication system centers on the voter's signed return identification envelope rather than presentation of photo ID at a polling place. Avoid saying Oregon has no identification requirements at all because identifying information is part of voter registration. The 2026 election calendar provides November 24 as the last day to resolve ballot challenges, including signature-related challenges.

accessible_voting.label: Accessible Voting
accessible_voting.content: Oregon provides voting assistance and accessible ballot options for voters with disabilities. A voter may ask a county elections office for help registering, marking or returning a ballot. Assistance may be provided by election staff or by another person chosen by the voter, except an employer, an agent of the employer or an officer or agent of a union of which the voter is a member. Oregon also provides accessible voting technology and alternative ballot-access methods so voters with disabilities can vote privately and independently. Ballots must still satisfy Oregon's Election Day return or mailing deadlines.
accessible_voting.glance_value: Accessible voting assistance and ballot options available
accessible_voting.source_name: Oregon Secretary of State — Services for Voters with Disabilities
accessible_voting.internal_note: The Secretary of State explicitly directs voters with disabilities to their county elections office for assistance and identifies restrictions on who may assist. Oregon's accessible-voting resources include alternative formats and voting technologies. Do not imply that an electronically marked ballot necessarily constitutes unrestricted online ballot return.

military_overseas.label: Military & Overseas Voting
military_overseas.content: Oregon provides special voting procedures for eligible uniformed-service members, qualifying family members and U.S. citizens living outside the United States. Ballots are sent to covered military and overseas voters at least 45 days before Election Day. Eligible voters may use Oregon's online ballot-marking tool and may receive voting materials through special military and overseas procedures. Oregon permits qualifying military and overseas voters to submit a voted ballot, signed return materials and the required Secret Ballot Waiver Form by fax or email. Covered voters must generally be registered at least 21 days before the election.
military_overseas.glance_value: Ballots sent at least 45 days before Election Day
military_overseas.source_name: Oregon Secretary of State — Military and Overseas Voters
military_overseas.internal_note: Oregon is notable because qualifying military and overseas voters may return ballots electronically by fax or email when they submit the required signed envelope and Secret Ballot Waiver Form. The Secretary of State directly confirms this procedure. For the November 3, 2026 election, the 45-day UOCAVA transmission point falls in September. The dedicated UOCAVA instructions should control over ordinary domestic ballot-return guidance.

student_voting.label: College / Student Voting
student_voting.content: College students may register in Oregon if they meet the state's voter eligibility and residency requirements. Students attending school away from their voting residence should make sure their voter registration and ballot mailing address are current. Oregon's vote-by-mail system allows a voter to maintain a residence address for voting purposes while providing a different mailing address for delivery of the ballot when appropriate. Students who move should update their registration or ballot mailing information through My Vote or their county elections office.
student_voting.glance_value: Keep residence and ballot mailing addresses current
student_voting.source_name: Oregon Secretary of State — Upcoming Elections
student_voting.internal_note: The Secretary of State's current election page specifically identifies student voters as a special voting circumstance and directs them to additional guidance. Because Oregon automatically mails ballots, the distinction between residence address and mailing address can be particularly important for students. Avoid implying that merely attending an Oregon college automatically establishes Oregon voting residency.

sample_ballot.label: Official Voters' Pamphlet & Ballot Information
sample_ballot.content: The Oregon Secretary of State publishes an official State Voters' Pamphlet for statewide elections, with candidate and measure information and accessible versions online. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, reviewed and compliant filings are scheduled to be available online September 18, the State Voters' Pamphlet is scheduled to be available online September 29, and printed pamphlets are scheduled for delivery to Oregon residences October 7 through October 9. Actual ballot contents vary by voting residence and local contests, so voters should review the ballot mailed to them and official county election information.
sample_ballot.source_name: Oregon Secretary of State — 2026 General Election Voters' Pamphlet
sample_ballot.internal_note: The Secretary of State has already published the November 3, 2026 Voters' Pamphlet schedule: unofficial filings August 31, reviewed filings September 18, State Voters' Pamphlet online September 29, audio guide October 5, printed delivery October 7-9 and translated state/county pamphlets online October 9. Reverify after September 29 when the official pamphlet becomes available.

contact.label: Contact the State Election Authority
contact.content: Oregon Secretary of State, Elections Division, Public Service Building, 255 Capitol St. NE, Suite 126, Salem, OR 97310. Phone: 503-986-1518. Toll-free: 866-673-VOTE (866-673-8683). Fax: 503-373-7414. TTY: 800-735-2900. For voter-specific registration, ballot delivery, replacement ballot, drop-site or ballot-status questions, contact your county elections office.
contact.source_name: Oregon Secretary of State — Elections Division
contact.internal_note: The Secretary of State's current election pages verify the Elections Division address, 503-986-1518, 866-673-8683, 503-373-7414 and 800-735-2900. County elections offices are responsible for mailing ballots and registering voters. No unverified email address was inserted. All contact information is plain text with no Markdown link syntax.

official_resources.label: Official State & Local Resources
official_resources.content: Use the Oregon Secretary of State Elections Division and My Vote for official statewide election information. My Vote allows voters to check and update registration, track ballot status, locate official ballot drop sites and find county elections office contact information. County elections offices register voters, mail ballots, issue replacement ballots, operate official drop sites and administer local election functions.
